title: Better typography
summary: How text renders: scale, spacing, features, wrapping, punctuation.

overview.purpose: Set and review how text renders, from the type scale to wrapping and punctuation.
overview.when: Building or reviewing any interface with text in it, before you call the type done.

sections.title: Measured, not preferred
sections.intro: Some values are exact findings; others are heuristics.

items.title: Exact values
items.text: Missing these is a finding.
items.more: Unitless line-height, weight 400+ below 18px, a 60–75 character measure, 16px inputs on iOS and tabular-nums on changing values.

items.title: Heuristics
items.text: Report only where they break the scale.
items.more: Letter-spacing, pairing and scale ratios. Never propose a new typeface unless the task asks for a type change.

sections.title: Fonts and weights
sections.intro: Weight and size carry hierarchy; each extra one dilutes it.

items.title: Three fonts at most
items.text: Apps fewer, marketing pages can carry more.
items.more: Pair for contrast: a serif headline over a sans body reads deliberate, two near-identical sans-serifs read as a mistake.

items.title: No thin text under 18px
items.text: Below 18px use weight 400 or heavier.
items.more: Weights 100–300 belong at 28px and up, checked against the background even there.

items.title: Load every face you use
items.text: Browsers fake missing weights and italics.
items.more: Synthesized faces distort the design. Disable synthesis only after checking the fallback stack, and only the unwanted mode.
items.css:
/* only after the fallback stack is checked */
body { font-synthesis-weight: none; }

items.title: Properties over raw tags
items.text: font-weight, not font-variation-settings.
items.more: Properties keep working when a non-variable fallback renders. Leave font-optical-sizing at auto. Raw tags only for custom axes and features with no property.

sections.title: Scale and spacing
sections.intro: A small set of sizes, each paired with its line-height and weight.

items.title: A type scale with roles
items.text: One role = one decision, not three.
items.more: Define few sizes and deviate rarely. On a team, name sizes by use (text-body-sm) so the rules survive.

items.title: Headings descend with level
items.text: A subheading never overpowers its parent.
items.more: Deep levels may share a size if weight or tracking keeps them distinct. A heading is never smaller than body text unless it is a deliberate overline.

items.title: Line-height by role
items.text: Display 1.1, headings 1.2–1.3, body 1.5–1.6.
items.more: Use unitless values so line-height scales with size. Anything that wraps to three lines or more needs at least 1.4.

items.title: Letter-spacing by size
items.text: Tighten big headings, open small caps.
items.more: Headings 24px+ take −0.01 to −0.02em. Uppercase labels at 14px or smaller take 0.05em. Body stays at 0. Never turn kerning off.

items.title: Size floors
items.text: Body 16px, UI 14px, captions 13px.
items.more: Rarely go below 12px. Set font-size in rem so the reader’s browser setting still applies.

items.title: Trim text boxes
items.text: Text sits low in buttons and badges.
items.more: text-box trims the space a font reserves above and below its letters. A progressive enhancement.

sections.title: Wrapping and measure
sections.intro: Decide where lines break instead of leaving it to chance.

items.title: Cap the measure
items.text: 60–75 characters per line.
items.more: Any unit works as long as a cap exists and the line length lands in range.

items.title: Balance headings
items.text: Even lines for headings and short text.
items.more: Never on paragraphs; Chromium ignores it past six lines.

items.title: Pretty paragraphs
items.text: No lone word on the last line.
items.more: Safe on any paragraph, long-form included.

items.title: Let long words break
items.text: Links and IDs stay in their box.
items.more: Use overflow-wrap where a long word, link or ID could escape the container.

items.title: Keep labels on one line
items.text: nowrap where a break looks broken.
items.more: Labels and badges. Keep interface text at text-align: start; justify is for editorial layouts only.

items.title: Truncate with a way back
items.text: Ellipsis plus a path to the full text.
items.more: One line: overflow, text-overflow and nowrap. Several: -webkit-box with line-clamp.
items.css:
.one { overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
.three { display: -webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 3; overflow: hidden; }

sections.title: Numbers, punctuation, details
sections.intro: The small things readers notice without knowing why.

items.title: Tabular numbers
items.text: Timers, counters, prices and columns.
items.more: Every digit keeps one width so nothing shifts. Leave figures in prose proportional.

items.title: Typographic punctuation
items.text: Curly quotes, en dashes, the ellipsis.
items.more: Never keyboard stand-ins in rendered text: “ ” not " ", – for ranges, … not ..., non-breaking spaces where needed. Code keeps straight quotes.

items.title: Natural case
items.text: Set case with text-transform.
items.more: Store text in natural case so a redesign never means rewriting copy.

items.title: Underlines from the font
items.text: Let the font place the underline.
items.more: Or tune offset and thickness by hand. A dotted style hints at extra information, like an abbreviation.
items.css:
a { text-underline-position: from-font; text-decoration-thickness: from-font; }
abbr { text-decoration-style: dotted; }

items.title: Inputs at 16px on mobile
items.text: iOS zooms below 16px.
items.more: Either size the input up on small screens, or keep 16px and scale it down visually. Ask which the design wants.

items.title: Smoothing once, on the root
items.text: Never per component.
items.more: Apply both vendor properties once on the root element.

items.title: Language and direction
items.text: Set lang and dir.
items.more: Browsers pick quotes, hyphenation and pronunciation from lang. Wrap mixed-direction values in a bdi element.

items.title: Decorative text in CSS
items.text: Not in images.
items.more: Drop caps, outlines and shadows in CSS keep text selectable and searchable.

items.title: Keep text selectable
items.text: user-select: none only on drag surfaces.
items.more: ::selection can carry the brand as long as the pair stays legible.

sections.title: Before you finish
sections.intro: Run these before calling the type done.
items: Every font-weight has a loaded face
No font-synthesis: none on body text
balance on headings, pretty on paragraphs
Font smoothing only on the root
